scope: plugins/planning (the interview skill, its shared context and reference, and the scripts it calls)
counts: 5 owners of the register status set
top_why: Two parsers already read the same ledger differently, so this is a live defect, and two other candidates build on its register module.

candidates.title: Give the ledger register one owner
candidates.problem: The register grammar is implemented in bash, again in Python, listed in a JSON schema and in two prose files, and the copies disagree.
candidates.solution: One ledger-grammar module owns the section locator, fence rule, row grammar and status table; the gate and the page merge become its callers.
wins: locality: a new status, one edit
candidates.verified: corrected: Python returns three rows on a nested fence, not one

candidates.title: State the gate contract once
candidates.problem: The gate commands, exit codes and carve-outs are restated in six places, and the hub announces that the copies must be kept in sync.
candidates.solution: One Gate before locking section owns the commands, exit codes and carve-outs; every other place keeps a one-line pointer.

candidates.title: Give each interview step one owner
candidates.problem: loop.md mirrors the hub's step skeleton, so each step's contract is split between a hub summary, a loop.md detail and the checklist.
candidates.solution: Each step lives in one place: the hub keeps when, halts and outputs, and one spoke per phase holds the mechanics.
wins: interface: hub reads as step list
candidates.verified: corrected: nine is the required heading set, consistent today

after.caption: hub: when, halts, outputs · spoke: mechanics

candidates.title: Stop copying the sweep enum into the checklist
candidates.problem: The checklist template restates the assumption sweep's categories and disposition rule, and both copies are already wrong.
candidates.solution: The template keeps the section skeleton and example rows and points to the module that owns each enum.
wins: leverage: every new ledger stays current

before.caption: 7 kinds vs a stale copy of 5

candidates.title: Merge the two page-lane files
candidates.problem: The registry always loads lane-page.md and surface.md together, and the pair restates the exit codes, degrade conditions and start command.
candidates.solution: One page-lane module states exit codes, the degrade rule and the start command once, and a shared file holds the wake payload both lanes read.
wins: locality: exit codes in one file

candidates.title: Fold acceptance-criteria capture into one module
candidates.problem: coverage-prompt.md and ears.md share one trigger and one concept, and the hub restates the coverage exemption five times.
candidates.solution: One acceptance-criteria module owns the coverage prompt, the EARS tags and the format pointer; the hub keeps one sentence.
wins: locality: exemption wording in one file

nodes.label: acceptance-criteria module: coverage prompt and EARS tags

candidates.title: Make the shared planning modules complete
candidates.problem: The hub and loop.md copy the source order and the consequential definition, and the interview uses an outcome self-answer.md never defines.
candidates.solution: self-answer.md owns every answered-from outcome, and the hub and loop.md cite sections and state only their delta.
wins: leverage: three skills share one definition

candidates.title: Fold relentless-mode.md into the hub
candidates.problem: A nine-line spoke on the default path holds one framing paragraph the hub already states.
candidates.solution: The hub keeps the framing sentence under a mode-neutral heading, and the spoke is deleted.
wins: interface: one file fewer to load

before.caption: pointer as long as the spoke

candidates.title: Load only the per-round routing check
candidates.problem: Size and fog routing is split across five files, and each round loads all 131 lines of routing.md for about 34 of them.
candidates.solution: routing.md owns the scope cut, and the per-round check sits apart from the entry and handoff parts.
wins: locality: routing rule in one file
interface: rounds load the check only

candidates.title: Move nfr-prompts.md to the shared context
candidates.problem: prd and design link into the interview's private context folder, past its interface.
candidates.solution: nfr-prompts.md lives in the plugin-level context folder beside problem-framing.md, with a check that no skill links into another's context.
wins: leverage: three skills, one shared file

candidates.title: Quote config defaults from one table
candidates.problem: lane-shared.md re-tabulates the shared-session keys and defaults config.md holds, and the hub restates defaults beside its pointers.
candidates.solution: config.md owns every key and default, and interview prose cites it without quoting a value.

candidates.title: Keep one skill-to-skill edge table
candidates.problem: Where the interview sends the user next is listed in composition.md, handoff.md, the hub's Next section and its intake list.
candidates.solution: composition.md holds the single edge table with triggers, and handoff.md keeps only the task-shape logic.
wins: interface: hub Next names one file

candidates.title: Pull interview state out of the server
candidates.problem: State derivation lives in the HTTP server module, and offline commands import it through sys.path edits.
candidates.solution: A pure interview-state module owns state derivation, and the server becomes a transport adapter over it.
wins: leverage: three callers, one state module

candidates.title: Emit and verify the Brief in one place
candidates.problem: Brief emission is Python and Brief verification is a bash script that shells out to the emitter and re-parses its output with awk.
candidates.solution: One check-brief command owns emitting and verifying the Brief against a single heading constant.

candidates.title: Give every asking lane the question shape
candidates.problem: question-shape.md carries 45 lines only the shared lane needs, yet the page and shared lanes' read lists omit it.
candidates.solution: lane-shared.md owns the shared-lane field table, and every asking lane's registry read list names question-shape.md.
wins: interface: registry, not prose, loads it
locality: shared fields with their lane

candidates.title: Move each gotcha beside its rule
candidates.problem: Most gotchas restate a rule another module owns, and the hub's pointer to the file carries no read condition.
candidates.solution: Each failure rationale sits beside the rule it explains, and only entries with no other home stay.

candidates.title: Keep page-lane commands out of the hub
candidates.problem: The hub says it names no lane, yet it spells out round.sh subcommands the page-lane files own.
candidates.solution: The page-lane module owns its round.sh subcommands, and the hub states each step's outcome only.
wins: locality: lane commands in one module

after.caption: subcommands live in the page lane module

candidates.title: Own the variation-intent vocabulary once
candidates.problem: The variation-intent question, its Brief line and a stumble note are stated in three files that disagree on two parts versus three.
candidates.solution: variation-points.md owns the vocabulary and the Brief line, and the interview and design cite it.
wins: locality: one definition of the question

candidates.title: Make cited sections real headings
candidates.problem: Five references cite an In-flight lookups section that is a bold lead-in buried in a 2,293-character paragraph.
candidates.solution: Every section other files cite is a real heading, with a lint that each quoted section name resolves.
wins: locality: readers land on the rule
candidates.verified: corrected: the pointer exists but is buried, not broken

candidates.title: Join the stop-boundary spokes
candidates.problem: handoff.md and session-config.md fire at the same boundary, and the hub lists session-config.md's table of contents.
candidates.solution: One stop-boundary module with two sections sits behind a single hub pointer.
wins: locality: stop guidance in one file

candidates.title: Shrink hub pointers to trigger and link
candidates.problem: Hub bullets carry their spoke's rule, so the pointer says as much as the file it points to.
candidates.solution: Each hub line holds a trigger and a pointer, and the spoke alone holds the rule.
wins: locality: rule text in one file

candidates.title: Split the gate script into subcommands
candidates.problem: Four gates share one flag-driven command and one exit code, and the prose encodes their internal ordering.
candidates.solution: Gate subcommands make the ordering part of the interface, done together with the register and Brief modules.

candidates.title: Check op fields against the schema
candidates.problem: Each op's fields are declared in OP_ARGS, the ops schema and a markdown table, and only op names are tested for agreement.
candidates.solution: OP_ARGS field sets are generated from, or checked against, the ops schema.
wins: locality: op field change, one place
